Here are focused things to look for when shopping for an electric guitar, based on the Strat vs Les Paul differences you mentioned:

- Body shape & construction: try both body styles (contoured Strat vs single-cut Les Paul) to see which feels comfortable sitting or standing.
- Neck & scale: check neck profile and scale length (Strat typically 25.5" vs Les Paul 24.75"); see which neck thickness and length suit your fretting hand.
- Electronics: compare pickup types and switching — Strats commonly have three single-coils and a 5-way switch; Les Pauls have two humbuckers and a 3-way toggle. Pickups strongly affect tone and noise.
- Tone: listen for the overall character — Strats are described as brighter and more articulate; Les Pauls warmer, fuller, and more sustaining. Play chords and leads you normally use to judge.
- Playability: try fretting and bending across the neck; comfort can differ with neck shape and body contours.
- Weight: feel the guitar plugged in and unplugged — Les Pauls are typically heavier than Strats and that can affect long sessions.
- Budget & value: compare prices for the models you like (they often differ by several hundred dollars); factor in cases, setup, and accessories.

A final tip from the comparison: try both guitars through an amp you’d use live or at home, and choose the one that feels right in your hands and with the tone you prefer.
